items.question: Rule the boundary PROPOSAL (boss adoption required): merge 12:1-6 into one petition-and-reply row. ADOPT with exact merged span/unit_type/parent + which row retires + tiling consequence, or DECLINE.

P04-011.challenge_claim: Two challenges land here: that the cut before verse 5 separates the complaint from the reply it draws at a join carrying no tier-1 device, with a treachery catchword straddling that seam undisclosed; and that the opening warrant's new-first-person-voice reading is contradicted by dispute, testing and kidneys vocabulary tying 12:1-3 back across the opening seam to 11:20, likewise undisclosed.
P04-011.grounds: Distinct defects at opposite edges of one row; both are real, and one framing needs correction. Opening edge: 11:18-20 is already first-person prophetic speech -- הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה at oshb:Jer.11.18 (byte) and גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) -- so the first person at 12:1 RESUMES across the intervening koh-amar reply rather than opening a new voice, and the warrant as written is byte-false. The ties verify on their named objects, not merely their digits: אָרִ֖יב at oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte; that form, sweep: 2 verses) answers רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte; sweep: 3 verses); the kidneys token stands at בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב in oshb:Jer.11.20 and at מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם in oshb:Jer.12.2 (both byte; that token, sweep: 4 verses); and וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י at oshb:Jer.12.3 (byte; sweep: 3 verses) answers the testing participle of oshb:Jer.11.20 (sweep: 3 verses). Closing edge: 12:5 opens כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (byte) with no messenger, attribution or word-event formula, and the nearest koh-amar-YHWH sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between; כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד closes oshb:Jer.12.1 while בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ stands in oshb:Jer.12.6 (both byte), the family's only two sites in chapters 10-13 (bare consonantal substring, sweep: 12 verses) -- a byte-true catchword crossing this row's own closing seam, undisclosed. Three corrections to the closing-seam framing: an argument resting on the ABSENCE of a paragraph mark at the verse-4/5 join is barred, that layer being tier-3 in the Prophets with absence never counterevidence; the marks do not merely flank the proposed six-verse exchange, since a setumah stands at MT 12:3 inside it (single-witness, tier-3, and the row does disclose it); and כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד is verse-final at 12:1, not the complaint's opening. The cut itself survives on ground the row never argues: 12:1-4 names its addressee, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), while 12:5-6 addresses the one whose brothers and father's house are in view -- a byte-visible addressee-referent shift, which is a ruled seam class.
P04-011.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the new-first-person-voice wording with the byte-shown resumption of the first-person voice standing at 11:18-20 across the koh-amar reply of 11:21-23, and ground the cut before verse 5 on the addressee-referent shift read off the pointed bytes (YHWH named as addressee in 12:1-4; the prophet's own brothers and father's house as addressee in 12:5-6) rather than on the absence of a formula. device_notes: disclose BOTH straddling device sets with swept object and verse count -- the dispute, testing and kidneys ties running back to 11:20, and the treachery catchword running forward to 12:6. Delete any sentence resting on a paragraph mark being absent. Boundary PROPOSAL (boss adoption required; not author work): merge 12:1-6 into one petition-and-reply row. Test the cure must pass: the warrant states each half's addressee from the pointed bytes; every device straddling either of the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no evidentiary sentence rests on marker absence.

row.boundary_rationale: A dispute addressed directly to Yahweh opens the unit, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָרִ֖יב אֵלֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), matching “You are righteous, Yahweh, when I contend with you;” (web:Jer.12.1) — a new first-person voice against the judgment oracle that closes the previous chapter. The complaint presses the question directly, “Why does the way of the wicked prosper?” (web:Jer.12.1), and continues through the land's mourning and the wicked's own boast that they won't see Jeremiah's latter end. The row is cut before verse 5 because the addressee there turns around: second person switches from naming Yahweh to naming Jeremiah himself, without any formula marking the change.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this unit through Yahweh's reply that follows was rejected because the addressee plainly turns around at verse 5, from Jeremiah speaking to Yahweh to Yahweh speaking to Jeremiah, even though no koh-amar or other formula marks that turn.
row.literature_type_guess: complaint over the prosperity of the wicked
row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
row.device_notes: A setumah closes the preceding chapter at oshb:Jer.11.23 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), just before this unit's own opening dispute; a further setumah sits inside the span at oshb:Jer.12.3, neither driving the boundary argued above. The dispute vocabulary opening the unit — contend, plead a case — echoes courtroom language without turning the unit into a distinct legal speech; it is held here as the register of the complaint itself.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The speaking voice turns from Jeremiah's own prayer back to Yahweh's, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עַל אַנְשֵׁ֣י עֲנָת֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life,” (web:Jer.11.21), naming the men of Anathoth who threaten the prophet's life. A second therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause follows immediately, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte) — “The young men will die by the sword.” (web:Jer.11.22) — but carries the same speaker forward rather than introducing a new one, so it intensifies the sentence rather than opening a fresh unit. The three verses stand together as Yahweh's reply and close the chapter.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the second therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause in verse 22 as its own row was rejected because it carries forward the same speaker announcing judgment on the same named opponents, rather than a change of who is speaking.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: A setumah closes the preceding unit at oshb:Jer.11.20 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), just before this unit's own opening verse, which itself carries a further setumah at oshb:Jer.11.21; a third closes the unit and the chapter at oshb:Jer.11.23. The three marks do not drive the one-speaker reading of the doubled clause disclosed above.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The addressee turns around without any introducing formula: כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte), matching “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses?” (web:Jer.12.5), reads as Yahweh's own reply to the complaint just voiced, now naming Jeremiah as the one addressed rather than the one speaking. The reply closes with a warning against Jeremiah's own household, אַל תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) — “Don’t believe them, though they speak beautiful words to you.” (web:Jer.12.6). The row is cut before verse 7 because the voice there turns again, to Yahweh speaking of forsaking my house rather than replying to Jeremiah.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 5-6 as a continuation of Jeremiah's own complaint rather than Yahweh's reply was rejected because the addressee is named in the second person across both verses as the one who runs, whose brothers and father's house are in view — Jeremiah's own circumstances rather than Yahweh's.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Yahweh's reply to the complaint, warning against Jeremiah's own household
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: A setumah closes this short span at oshb:Jer.12.6 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration), texture rather than a driver for the boundary. No formula marks the turn from complaint to reply at verse 5, so the two-verse span is held at reduced confidence honestly rather than forced to a firmer reading.

items.question: Rule the proposed split at 15:19 (peer: boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption). ADOPT with exact spec, or DECLINE.

P05-014.challenge_claim: The stated ground for declining a cut at 15:19 is byte-false: the divine reply is not already underway there, because 15:15-18 is the prophet's own voice, so the verse-initial koh-amar does carry a change of speaking mouth; two ketiv/qere notes inside the span are also undisclosed.
P05-014.grounds: The premise fails on the span's own bytes. The reply opening at MT 15:11 runs to MT 15:14; MT 15:15 turns to the prophet addressing the deity, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier) -- a vocative divine name standing between a second-person-singular verb and two imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- and the first-person complaint holds through MT 15:16-15:18, both witnesses rendering those four verses in the prophet's mouth. So the formula at לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) resumes divine speech after four verses in the other mouth: the mouth carrying the formula does change there, and the row's reason for declining the cut -- that it brings no change of frame-owner from a reply already underway -- is contradicted by the bytes it cites. Under the ruled granularity a koh-amar onset WITH a frame-owner change is a licensed internal seam, so what the row sets aside as a non-event is a live seam candidate. The mark arm verifies as well: two variant notes fall inside Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21, at MT 15:11 -- שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), the verse cited as the reply's onset -- and at MT 15:16, inside the complaint; neither is disclosed. Independently re-verified and NOT defective: the row's 8-verse digit for the alef-initial outcry lexeme matches the byte-derived count object exactly (8 verses, MT keys), while a bare consonantal substring sweep on the same three letters returns 14 verses, contaminated by the enemy and fool bases -- the digit is true only under the token-bound object the row names, and it names it. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 15:10, 15:14, 15:16, 15:17, 15:18; petuchah at MT 15:21; the two types never conflated). High stands: the defect sits in the clause that carries the row's whole hold-together argument.
P05-014.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative and the matching boundary_rationale clause: rewrite on a true premise -- the divine reply does not run unbroken from 15:11; it breaks at 15:15 where the prophet's voice resumes, and the formula at 15:19 opens a second divine reply with a changed speaking mouth. Any ground for holding Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 whole must then be argued from the complaint-and-reply exchange as one scene under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule, not from a continuous reply. device_notes: add the single-witness ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 15:11 and MT 15:16. Splitting at 15:19 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption -- never author work. Cure test: a per-verse mouth check across Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 must sustain every voice statement the prose makes, and every in-span variant verse must be named.

row.boundary_rationale: “Woe is me, my mother” (web:Jer.15.10) opens אֽוֹי לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) -- another oy apostrophe (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, the same lexeme spliced at 13:27 above), here turned inward as Jeremiah's own outcry rather than a judgment against the city, a clean scene shift from the divine judgment speech just closed. Yahweh's reply opens at 15:11 without a further addressee change (private dialogue continues), and a second reply opens “Therefore Yahweh says” (web:Jer.15.19) on לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) -- a koh-amar with no change of frame-owner, so it does not itself open a fresh row. Complaint and reply run together to the closing promise of deliverance at 15:21.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at 15:19's koh-amar onset, or at 15:11 where the voice turns from Jeremiah's complaint to Yahweh's reply, was considered and set aside: the confession's complaint-and-reply dialogue holds one scene and one addressee pair, Jeremiah and Yahweh, from complaint to reply, and 15:19's koh-amar does not change the frame-owner from the reply already underway.
row.literature_type_guess: individual complaint-and-reply dialogue between Jeremiah and Yahweh

prev_row.boundary_rationale: “For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem?” (web:Jer.15.5) turns to second-feminine-singular direct address, כִּ֠י מִֽי יַחְמֹ֤ל עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.15.5, byte tier) -- Jerusalem addressed by name rather than by the third-person language of 15:1-4. The poem moves between that direct address (15:5-6) and third-person description of the widows and the destroyer (15:7-9) without a further scene change, closing on the neum-YHWH formula at 15:9.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row where the grammar shifts from second-person address (15:5-6) to third-person description (15:7-9) was considered: Hebrew poetry moves between address and description within one sustained poem routinely, so no fresh row was opened there.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: direct-address dirge over Jerusalem's bereaved widows

next_row.boundary_rationale: A word-event opens the unit: “Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.16.1), rendering vayehi debar-YHWH וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.16.1, byte tier) -- one of the book's narrative word-event onsets. The command that follows, “You shall not take a wife” (web:Jer.16.2), opens on לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.2, byte tier), and two further commands in the same voice and to the same addressee follow without a scene change: “Don’t enter into the house of mourning” (web:Jer.16.5) and “You shall not go into the house of feasting” (web:Jer.16.8), the marriage and the mourning commands paired with their own koh-amar rationale (16:3-4, 16:6-7), and the feasting command with the full divine-name stack “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says”, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier). The three prohibitions and their rationales stay one row because no addressee or scene shift interrupts the sequence -- Jeremiah is the one hearer named across the span, and the koh-amar onsets explain the command just given rather than opening a new frame-owner.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:1-9 as a symbolic_act_report alongside the book's other enacted signs was considered and set aside: the span pairs its three prohibitions with their own rationale without narrating Jeremiah's own compliance in a first-person performance clause the way the potter's-house sign that opens the next frame does (web:Jer.18.3), so the material was kept in command-and-rationale form as judgment_oracle.
next_row.literature_type_guess: sign-oracle: paired command-and-rationale prohibitions barring marriage, mourning, and feasting
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

Inside the row's own span, Jer.16.4 carries a further setumah and Jer.16.8 carries a further setumah. (tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets, disclosed single-witness). Both interior breaks fall inside a prohibition rather than between two of them.

P06-004.challenge_claim: The opening at 16:16 names no seam from any of the six ruled tier-1 classes; the cut from 16:14-15 rests on a change of imagery alone, with no addressee or grammatical-person shift to ground it.
P06-004.grounds: The substance is upheld on bytes; two framing elements are wrong. UPHELD: no person or addressee change separates the two sides of this seam. MT 16:15 closes on third-person-plural reference, וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.15, byte tier), and MT 16:16 keeps the same third-person-plural referents in the same divine mouth, וְדִיג֑וּם (oshb:Jer.16.16, byte tier), through the recompense clause at עֲוֺנָם֙ וְחַטָּאתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.18, byte tier); no participant, location or hearer changes across the cut, so the declared scene-shift signal is not byte-carried and what actually turns is the imagery, from return-promise to pursuit. That continuity is a byte-true device straddling the row's own opening seam and is nowhere disclosed, which under the cross-seam cohesion rule argues continuity against the cut until the row faces it; and the rival the row actually rejects is only the easier forward pairing with the trust-hymn at 16:19-21, never the backward join that shares mouth, referents and person. CORRECTED FRAMING: the row does name one of the ruled classes -- the defect is that the named class fails on the bytes, not that none is named; and the comparandum offered against it is byte-false, since the onset at MT 16:14 is a hinneh plus days-are-coming announcement while MT 16:16 opens on a first-person presentative plus participle, different constructions with different opening forms. Credited and not disturbed: the one variant note in the span, at MT 16:16 on the fishermen noun (sweep: 1 note in MT 16:16-16:18), is disclosed and correctly located, and the splice stops before it; parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed. Medium stands: both declared signals and the rejected-rival ground are affected while the row carries high confidence.
P06-004.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace narrative_frame.scene_shift with a signal the bytes carry at 16:16, or hold the seam on disclosed grounds instead -- a content reversal from return-promise to pursuit, with the third-person-plural continuity across the seam disclosed against the row per the cross-seam cohesion rule and the tier-3 mark at MT 16:15 cited as corroboration only, never as driver. strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite it to test the backward join with 16:14-15 rather than the forward pairing with 16:19-21. confidence: re-open with the driver swap. Merging 16:16-18 into the preceding row is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption -- never author work. Cure test: the seam must survive a cross-seam cohesion check with the straddling third-person continuity disclosed, and the rejected rival must be the one the bytes make hardest to reject.

The pursuit imagery of fishermen and hunters (16:16-17) runs into the sentence “First I will recompense their iniquity and their sin double” (web:Jer.16.18), וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֣י רִֽאשׁוֹנָ֗ה מִשְׁנֵ֤ה עֲוֺנָם֙ וְחַטָּאתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.18, byte tier), closing the pollution-of-the-land charge as one address about “them” rather than to Yahweh.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row to include the trust-hymn that follows (16:19-21) was considered: both concern Yahweh's dealings with a plural “them,” but 16:19 turns to Jeremiah's own direct address to Yahweh, a speaker change kept as a fresh row.

The promise turns to a new-exodus return “from the land of the north” that closes “I will bring them again into their land that I gave to their fathers” (web:Jer.16.15), וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָֽם (oshb:Jer.16.15, byte tier).

next_row.boundary_rationale: “Yahweh, my strength, my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of affliction” (web:Jer.16.19) opens יְהוָ֞ה עֻזִּ֧י וּמָעֻזִּ֛י וּמְנוּסִ֖י בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.19, byte tier) -- a direct praise-address from Jeremiah to Yahweh, a speaker and addressee change from the third-person pursuit oracle just closed. items.question: Rule the proposed respan folding 17:12-13 into the petition (peer: BOUNDARY PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the remedy cures the row as spanned). ADOPT with exact spec, or DECLINE.

P06-008.challenge_claim: The two-verse doxology cut leaves a byte-true catchword bond undisclosed: the shaming verb on which the row's closing splice ends at 17:13 recurs at 17:18, bracketing the petition that follows and arguing that 17:12-13 belongs with that petition rather than standing as its own unit; the tier-3 segmentation also groups 17:11-13, so the opening seam falls inside a single marked segment.
P06-008.grounds: Re-derived from bytes.
